prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1190; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle was turning left when it struck a vehicle traveling straight through on the opposite approach. Claimant reports neck strain and is seeking medical evaluation. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Scheduled initial recorded statement from both parties.

Entry 2: Recorded statement obtained from insured. Insured states the left-turn signal had turned yellow and they proceeded when the gap appeared to be clear. Insured acknowledges not seeing the oncoming vehicle until impact. Photos of both vehicles and the intersection requested from insured.

Entry 3: Claimant contacted by phone. Claimant confirms neck pain and stiffness beginning the day of the accident, with no prior history of neck complaints. Claimant has seen a primary care provider and was given a diagnosis of cervical strain. Requested medical records and itemized bills. Explained the claims process; claimant has not asked about legal representation.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos and vehicle damage estimates. Damage to the claimant's vehicle is consistent with a broadside impact on the driver's side rear quarter. Independent appraisal assigned. Intersection traffic camera footage requested from the municipality; retention window noted as limited, so request marked urgent.

Entry 5: Received partial medical records. Treatment consists of initial exam, prescribed muscle relaxants, and a referral to physical therapy. Prognosis documented as favorable with expected recovery in several weeks. Liability assessment currently leaning toward insured based on left-turn yield obligation. Reserve reviewed and updated. Follow-up with claimant scheduled to confirm therapy attendance.
